7vo4tu:867: From Code to Molecules series: An AI-driven EGFR inhibitor discovery journey — a deep dive into scientific activities in the life and health industry through the deep integration of AWS Bedrock and Claude Code/Claude Agent Skills by awschina on 09 Feb 2026 in Industries Permalink Share The "three mountains" of traditional drug R&D Before delving into the topic of this article, let us first confront the brutal reality of the drug R&D field: Time cost: the lengthy R&D cycle From target discovery to clinical trials, the average R&D cycle of a new drug is as long as 10–15 years The early drug discovery stage (target validation → lead compound screening → optimization) alone requires 3–5 years Chemists must manually search the literature, download data, analyze compound properties, and draw structural diagrams; every step is a black hole of time Economic cost: astronomical investment The average R&D cost of a new drug is as high as $2.6 billion (Data source: Tufts CSDD, 2020) About 30% of the cost is spent on "trial and error" during the early drug discovery stage Large amounts of funding are wasted on compound screening with a low success rate (success rate below 5%) Skill barriers: the complexity of multidisciplinary intersection Medicinal chemists need to master: cheminformatics (RDKit), molecular docking (AutoDock), data analysis (Python), and literature management (EndNote) Data formats between different tools are incompatible and require manual conversion (e.g., SDF→PDB→MOL2) The problem of knowledge silos is severe: compound databases (ChEMBL), gene mutation databases (COSMIC), and literature databases (PubMed) are scattered across different platforms and cannot be automatically linked From pain points to breakthroughs: the Claude Agent Skills solution This is exactly the core focus of this article: How can a single prompt enable AI to automatically complete all of the above work? The traditional workflow requires repeatedly switching tools and manually processing data — the "grunt work" — which can now be handed over to AI for one-click completion.
